newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel strengthens against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel strengthens against the dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Monday following the U.S. currency's slide on overseas markets, dealers said.
"Volume was high today as the business sector continued to convert foreign currency (into shekels) for mid-month tax payments," said Zahi Elias of Bank Leumi.
"The decline of the dollar abroad was the main reason for the shekel's rise and the Bank of Israel had to purchase $200 million to support the basket," Elias said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3660 shekels against 3.3730 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6529 shekels against 3.6510 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7244 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7295 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9970 shekels after 1.9784 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3660 shekels.
